bug_description.original: Crash Type: Container-overflow READ 4. Crash State: Exiv2::Photoshop::locateIrb -> Exiv2::Photoshop::setIptcIrb -> Exiv2::JpegBase::doWriteMetadata. Sanitizer: address (ASAN).
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: The staged 240-byte witness is admitted by Exiv2 and reaches `JpegBase::writeMetadata()`, which rescans the JPEG and concatenates the payloads of APP13 `Photoshop 3.0\0` segments into `psBlob`. Because `Photoshop::valid()` accepts that buffer as a complete Photoshop IRB stream, `doWriteMetadata()` calls `Photoshop::setIptcIrb()` to remove or rewrite IPTC IRBs. Inside `setIptcIrb()`, the loop advances `pos` from attacker-derived IRB location and length fields (`newPos + sizeHdr + sizeIptc + (sizeIptc & 1)`) but then recomputes the remaining buffer size with unchecked unsigned `sizePsData - pos`. On the witness, a parsed IRB advances `pos` past the logical end of `psBlob`; the subtraction wraps to a huge `size_t`, `locateIptcIrb()` is called on an already out-of-bounds pointer, and `locateIrb()` then calls `isIrb()`, where `memcmp(pPsData, i, 4)` performs the observed 4-byte AddressSanitizer container-overflow read. The staged patch fixes the exact obligation by computing the remainder with `Safe::add<long>` and rejecting negative results before each `locateIptcIrb()` call.

source.description: Copies attacker-controlled bytes from recognized APP13 `Photoshop 3.0\0` segments into the Photoshop IRB blob that is later reparsed by `setIptcIrb()`.
source.value_from: The staged 240-byte `poc` is accepted as JPEG by Exiv2 and contains APP13 segments whose payload prefix matches `Photoshop::ps3Id_` (`"Photoshop 3.0\0"`); this statement appends the bytes after each 16-byte APP13/PS3 header into `psBlob`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The loop recomputes the remaining Photoshop-buffer length with unsigned `sizePsData - pos` without first enforcing `pos <= sizePsData`; once attacker-controlled IRB lengths push `pos` past the end of `psBlob`, the subtraction wraps and reparsing continues from an out-of-bounds pointer.
root_cause.note: The staged fix replaces this raw subtraction with `Safe::add<long>(static_cast<long>(sizePsData), -static_cast<long>(pos))` and `enforce(nextSizeData >= 0, ErrorCode::kerCorruptedMetadata)` before each call.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `memcmp` reads 4 bytes from the out-of-bounds pointer supplied after the wrapped remaining-length calculation.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `AddressSanitizer: container-overflow READ of size 4` in `isIrb`, reached through `locateIrb -> locateIptcIrb -> setIptcIrb -> doWriteMetadata`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This parse step materializes the attacker-controlled IPTC IRB start pointer and length fields that are later folded into `pos`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The Photoshop IRB bytes copied into `psBlob` at step 1 are reparsed here; the resulting `record`, `sizeHdr`, and `sizeIptc` values feed the skip-loop arithmetic that eventually wraps the remaining-length subtraction.

parser_admitted.description: During the write-metadata rescan, the input must present an APP13 segment whose payload begins with `Photoshop 3.0\0`; only then does Exiv2 enter the Photoshop APP13 accumulation path that feeds `setIptcIrb()`.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation; the chain is grounded only in the staged vulnerable source, patch, saved AddressSanitizer traces, reproduction report, and static inspection of the staged `poc`.
Stage 02 did not execute the fixed tree, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains `false` even though `patch.diff` adds the missing non-negative remainder checks around `sizePsData - pos`.

The saved Stage 01 artifacts do not print the exact `sizeHdr` and `sizeIptc` numbers from the final failing `setIptcIrb()` iteration, so the trace can ground the unchecked-subtraction mechanism and the resulting out-of-bounds pointer, but not the precise numeric IRB lengths that produced the overshoot.

fine_trace.note: Source. For each APP13 segment whose payload begins with `Photoshop::ps3Id_`, `doWriteMetadata()` copies the attacker-controlled bytes after the 16-byte APP13/PS3 header into `psBlob`. This materializes the exact Photoshop IRB byte stream later reparsed on the crashing path.

The accumulated `psBlob` is accepted as a complete Photoshop IRB stream, so `foundCompletePsData` becomes true during the write-time rescan. That control state is what directly enables the later call into `setIptcIrb()`.
Because `foundCompletePsData || iptcData_.count() > 0` is true, `doWriteMetadata()` reparses the attacker-controlled `psBlob` with `setIptcIrb()` to remove or rewrite IPTC IRBs.

The first parse of the whole Photoshop blob finds an IPTC IRB and turns its start pointer into `sizeFront`, the byte offset where IPTC removal begins. This shows that the attacker-controlled `psBlob` still looks valid enough to contain a locatable IPTC record before the failing skip loop starts.

fine_trace.code:
size_t pos = sizeFront;
while (0 == Photoshop::locateIptcIrb(pPsData + pos, sizePsData - pos, &record, &sizeHdr, &sizeIptc)) {
fine_trace.note: The skip loop reparses suffixes of the same buffer to remove the current and later IPTC IRBs. Its remaining-length argument is computed as unsigned `sizePsData - pos`, so safety now depends on `pos` never exceeding `sizePsData`; the vulnerable code does not enforce that invariant.

fine_trace.code:
const auto newPos = static_cast<size_t>(record - pPsData);
pos = newPos + sizeHdr + sizeIptc + (sizeIptc & 1);
fine_trace.note: Inside the loop, the next starting offset is recomputed from the located record start plus the attacker-derived IRB header size and IPTC payload length. The failing witness drives this arithmetic past the logical end of `pPsData`, setting up the wrapped subtraction on the next loop test.

Root cause. On the next loop test, `pos` is already larger than `sizePsData`, so the unsigned subtraction wraps to a huge `size_t` and `locateIptcIrb()` is called on an out-of-bounds starting pointer instead of rejecting the malformed IRB layout. The patch adds a checked signed remainder here.

With the wrapped size from step 7, `locateIrb()`'s own range check also sees a large remaining length, so it calls `isIrb()` on the stale pointer even though it no longer points within the logical `psBlob` buffer.

Sink. `memcmp` performs a 4-byte read from the out-of-bounds pointer supplied by step 8. The saved ASan trace reports this as `AddressSanitizer: container-overflow READ of size 4`; the shadow bytes show the read starts 142 bytes into the reserved vector allocation created for `psBlob`, after only 141 logical bytes remain addressable.

poc.trigger: Feed the staged 240-byte witness to `fuzz-read-print-write`; after `ImageFactory::open`, `readMetadata()`, and `writeMetadata()`, the write-metadata rescan reaches `Photoshop::setIptcIrb()` and crashes in `Photoshop::isIrb()`.

format.name: JPEG APP13 Photoshop IRB
format.contract: A file that Exiv2 admits as JPEG and whose APP13 `Photoshop 3.0\0` segments concatenate into a Photoshop IRB blob accepted by `Photoshop::valid()`, while malformed IPTC IRB length fields in that blob make `setIptcIrb()` advance `pos` past the blob before the next `sizePsData - pos` subtraction.
